# core/tls13record.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/tls13record.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

The TLS 1.3 record layer with the
ChaCha20-Poly1305, AES-128-GCM or AES-256-GCM cipher suite (RFC 8446 section 5): a record carries one
message of one content type, padded and sealed under the key and IV of
core/tls13 with the record's sequence number.

What is proved: every access is in bounds, nothing leaks, a sealed record
is the 5-byte header, the message, the content type, the padding and the
16-byte tag (so its length is exact), and an opened message is shorter
than its record. Not proved: that the records are the standard's; the tests
check records made by another implementation (Python's `cryptography`) and
every single-bit change of a record being refused.

`import "core/tls13record.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/aes.bastio](core-aes.md), [core/endian.bastio](core-endian.md), [core/aesgcm.bastio](core-aesgcm.md), [core/chacha20.bastio](core-chacha20.md), [core/poly1305.bastio](core-poly1305.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md), [core/chacha20poly1305.bastio](core-chacha20poly1305.md), [core/sha256.bastio](core-sha256.md), [core/sha512.bastio](core-sha512.md), [core/hkdf.bastio](core-hkdf.md), [core/tls13.bastio](core-tls13.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`tls13_seal`](#tls13_seal) | The record that carries `plain` as a message of type `content_type`, followed by `pad` zero bytes (the sealed part, with its tag, may not be longer than 2^14 + 256 bytes), sealed under `key` (32 bytes) and `iv` (12 bytes) as record number `seq`. |
| [`tls13_open`](#tls13_open) | Opens `record` (a whole record, header included) as record number `seq`. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Types and constants

### `TlsRecord`

```bastio
struct TlsRecord { content_type: u8, data: Bytes }
```

A record that was opened: the content type (22 handshake, 23 application
data, 21 alert) and the message.

## Functions

### `tls13_seal`

```bastio
fn tls13_seal(suite: u64, key: &Bytes, iv: &Bytes, seq: u64, content_type: u8, plain: &Bytes, pad: u64) -> Bytes
  requires ((suite == 4867 && blen(key) == 32) || (suite == 4866 && blen(key) == 32) || (suite == 4865 && blen(key) == 16)) && blen(iv) == 12 && blen(plain) <= 16384 && blen(plain) + 1 + pad + 16 <= 16640
  ensures blen(result) == 5 + blen(plain) + 1 + pad + 16
```

The record that carries `plain` as a message of type `content_type`,
followed by `pad` zero bytes (the sealed part, with its tag, may not be
longer than 2^14 + 256 bytes), sealed under `key` (32 bytes) and `iv` (12
bytes) as record number `seq`.

Example:

```bastio
let key = balloc(32);
let iv = balloc(12);
let msg = bfrom("hello");
let rec = tls13_seal(4867, key, iv, 0, 23, msg, 0);
let n = blen(rec);
bfree(rec);
bfree(msg);
bfree(iv);
bfree(key);
if n != 5 + 5 + 1 + 16 { return 1; }
```

### `tls13_open`

```bastio
fn tls13_open(suite: u64, key: &Bytes, iv: &Bytes, seq: u64, record: &Bytes) -> Option[TlsRecord]
  requires ((suite == 4867 && blen(key) == 32) || (suite == 4866 && blen(key) == 32) || (suite == 4865 && blen(key) == 16)) && blen(iv) == 12 && blen(record) < 274877906944
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some.data) + 21 < blen(record)
```

Opens `record` (a whole record, header included) as record number `seq`:
its content type and message, or nothing if the header is not a TLS 1.3
record header, the length is wrong, the tag does not match, or there is no
content type in the plaintext (all zeros).

Example:

```bastio
let key = balloc(32);
let iv = balloc(12);
let msg = bfrom("hello");
let rec = tls13_seal(4867, key, iv, 7, 22, msg, 3);
let mut ok = false;
match tls13_open(4867, key, iv, 7, rec) {
  Option::Some(r) => {
    ok = r.content_type == 22 && bytes_eq_str(r.data, "hello");
    bfree(r.data);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(rec);
bfree(msg);
bfree(iv);
bfree(key);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

## Internals

### `tls13_aead_seal`

```bastio
fn tls13_aead_seal(suite: u64, key: &Bytes, nonce: &Bytes, aad: &Bytes, plain: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires ((suite == 4867 && blen(key) == 32) || (suite == 4866 && blen(key) == 32) || (suite == 4865 && blen(key) == 16)) && blen(nonce) == 12
  requires blen(aad) < 274877906944 && blen(plain) < 274877906944
  ensures blen(result) == blen(plain) + 16
```

Internal: seals `plain` with the AEAD of the cipher suite `suite` (4865
AES-128-GCM, 4866 AES-256-GCM, 4867 ChaCha20-Poly1305).

### `tls13_aead_open`

```bastio
fn tls13_aead_open(suite: u64, key: &Bytes, nonce: &Bytes, aad: &Bytes, sealed: &Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires ((suite == 4867 && blen(key) == 32) || (suite == 4866 && blen(key) == 32) || (suite == 4865 && blen(key) == 16)) && blen(nonce) == 12
  requires blen(aad) < 274877906944 && blen(sealed) < 274877906944
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) + 16 == blen(sealed)
```

Internal: opens `sealed` with the AEAD of the cipher suite `suite`.

### `tls13_header`

```bastio
fn tls13_header(n: u64) -> Bytes
  requires n < 65536
  ensures blen(result) == 5
```

Internal: the 5-byte header of a record whose sealed part is `n` bytes.
